question.text: The chapter records that the term 'Social Enterprise' was formally introduced in India in 1981 with the establishment of which organization?

answer.text: Ashoka — the global association of the world's leading social entrepreneurs

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 1.3, the term 'Social Enterprise' was formally introduced in India in 1981 with the establishment of Ashoka — the global association of the world's leading social entrepreneurs. Ashoka predates other Indian-market SE investors. The Trap: Options A, B, D are all funders of SEs but came later and are not the 1981 formal-introduction entity. Villgro and Intellecap are Indian-origin; Acumen Fund is global — but all post-date 1981. Cross-Exam Context: Historical anchor useful for context in Ch 2 (SSE Introduction) where the SSE timeline is outlined (Budget 2019-20 → SEBI framework 2022 → NSE/BSE SSE Sep 2022). Assessor's Pro-Tip: Knowing the lineage helps when benchmarking an SE's self-described 'social-entrepreneurship legacy'. Long-vintage SEs often have better longitudinal data for SROI baselines — a useful factor in your sampling plan.
